title: Close deterministic gameplay modeling gaps from SRD audit
description:
Finding sources:
- Codex readiness review: prose-only buckets still include about 210 magic items, 306 rules, 101 equipment records, 69 features, and 9 actions.
- Codex mechanical-keyword pass: 369 records with likely gameplay mechanics but no typed mechanics projection.
- ChatGPT review: conditions, actions, many creature traits/actions, spells, adventuring gear, magic items, and rules are present but not deterministic enough for gameplay tools.
- Fable observation: prose-only magic-item charge economies and regular-but-still-parse-required fields remain.

Policy:
- This is not optional future polish. The audit criterion includes deterministic tool usability and primary DM discoverability.
- Every category gets implementation, research, or explicit accepted non-issue closure.
notes:
2026-07-08 ADR 0017 adjustment: Close children using the compiler decision procedure. A category is not automatically required to implement a full engine subsystem here; acceptable closure is clause-level pack semantics plus one of: code-enforced evidence, model-adjudicated-supported disposition with registered primitives, explicit engine-pending hook/family binding, or documented design-blocked owner. Prefer structural parsers/shared semantic grammars for repeated language and source-grounded curated specs for irregular reviewed clause families; never hand-edit generated output.
Completion verification: canonical SRD pack regenerates byte-exactly; rules-pack audit reports 0 suspicious records; independent deep audit reports 0 findings; verify:worktree passes Biome, forced typecheck, and 4,533 passing tests (19 documented skips).
